28.11.0.en: 12 "But where shall wisdom be found? and where is the place of understanding? 13 Man knoweth not the price thereof; neither is it found in the land of the living. 14 The depth saith, It is not in me: and the sea saith, It is not with me.

28.11.2.en: and where is the place of understanding?" [12]

28.11.3.en: If the treasures of precious metals are hidden beneath the earth, how much more is the wisdom of God. Who can perceive by himself where it is, or from where he may acquire true understanding?

28.11.4.en: Wisdom is the treasure hidden within the Gospel. No man can enjoy it unless the Spirit of God shines upon him with His light and reveals to him the mysteries of the Word.

28.11.5.en: * True wisdom is the Gospel, the means of salvation through the Cross of Christ.

28.12.0.en: St. John Chrysostom "Man knoweth not the price thereof; neither is it found in the land of the living" [13].

28.12.1.en: Wisdom is the Second Hypostasis, "the wisdom of God." While we are still in the flesh, we cannot grasp the depths of the mystery of Wisdom or know the Person of Wisdom, since He is in the bosom of the Father. He became incarnate so that He might meet us, and we might meet Him in our world.

28.12.2.en: * Paul does not mean here (1 Cor 2:7) that he proclaims secret matters and riddles, but that the message he preaches was formerly hidden.

28.12.3.en: Theodoret, Bishop of Cyrus * Wisdom is not in a time or in a place, for time would mean that it came into being. But how could it be in time, when it is from the beginning? How could it be in a place, when it was with God? If anyone is searching for the Only-Begotten Son, then according to the sense of the Gospel He is in the bosom of the Father. Do you think that the bosom of the Father is a place? Do you seek to know how wisdom was born, when the man of prophecy says, "Man knoweth not the price thereof" (Job 28:13)? Do you think that its origin is among men, while Job says that it is not found among men? Do you ascribe wisdom to death, when it is that of which "the depth saith, It is not in me: and the sea saith, It is not with me" (Job 28:14)?

28.12.4.en: St. Ambrose * Paul testifies (1 Cor 2:7) that he was sent to proclaim the mystery of the wisdom which the rulers of this world do not know, and for this reason they are called foolish. The wisdom of God is hidden, because it is not words but power. It is impossible to speak of it in human expressions, but we believe in it by the power of the Spirit.

28.12.5.en: Ambrosiaster * "Neither is it found in the land of them that live delicately" [13]. What does the land signify in this phrase but the soul of man? The Psalmist says, "My soul thirsteth after thee, as a thirsty land" (Ps 143:6). But this wisdom cannot be found in the land of those who live in luxury, for the man who still feeds on the pleasures of this life is deprived of the perception of eternal wisdom.

28.13.0.en: "The depth saith, It is not in me: and the sea saith, It is not with me" [14].

28.13.1.en: It is as though nature, with all the creativity, beauty and possibilities within it, speaks with man and directs his gaze to the Creator as the source of true wisdom, so that man does not seek it from nature, nor from books, nor from events, but from God Himself.

28.13.2.en: St. Augustine sees that God made wisdom hidden, not because He wants to deprive us of it, but to arouse our longing for it so that we may seek it earnestly.

28.13.3.en: * "The depth saith, It is not in me: and the sea saith, It is not with me" [14]. Holy Scripture often personifies many lifeless things, for example, "The sea saith, It is not with me," and so on. "The depth saith, It is not in me," "The heavens declare the glory of God" (Ps 19:1). The command is also given to the sword (Zech 13:7), and the mountains and hills are asked about their skipping with joy (Ps 114:6). We do not make a pretext of any of these, although some of our predecessors used them as strong proof. Let us reckon that this expression was used of our Saviour Himself, the true Wisdom.

28.13.4.en: Father Gregory of Nazianzus * When Job was asked about the place of wisdom he answered, "The depth saith, It is not in me," pointing not to the place where it is found, but to the place where it is not.

28.14.0.en: Again, when he said that its price is not known by man [15], and then went on, "It cannot be gotten for gold," he did not show what its price is, but what is not its price. It is clear to all that no man can find this wisdom in any place, nor buy it with riches. But the holy man, being full of mystical thoughts, leads us to discover other matters; he does not seek created wisdom, but the Wisdom who is the Creator. For unless we search the hidden depths of the symbolism in these words, what is said would certainly be of no value if it were interpreted from the historical side alone...

28.14.1.en: So then, what is the wisdom that the holy man contemplates but that of which the Apostle Paul says, "Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God" (1 Cor 1:24)?

28.14.2.en: Solomon wrote of her, "Wisdom hath builded her house" (Prov 9:1). And the Psalmist says of her, "In wisdom hast thou made them all" (Ps 104:24). Of this very Wisdom, "man knoweth not the price thereof" (c), for he finds nothing by which he can value it... There is no means of obtaining it...

28.14.3.en: What do we give so that we may be worthy to receive this Wisdom, who is Christ? For by grace we are saved... Man deserves one thing by way of justice (namely death), and receives another by grace... Paul says, "While we were yet sinners, Christ died for the ungodly in due time" (Rom 5:8, 6). So we who were found ungodly when Wisdom came, what good thing did we offer by which to receive this Wisdom? "Man knoweth not the price thereof" (c)... "For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: not of works, lest any man should boast" (Eph 2:8-9). And he speaks of himself, saying, "But by the grace of God I am what I am" (1 Cor 15:10).

28.14.4.en: * To what does the "sea" point but to worldly minds that suffer bitter turmoil, so that they enter into foolish hostility with others, and proceed in enmity from one person to another in turn, and minds shatter one another like waves dashing against each other? Rightly the life of worldly persons is called a sea, because it is in a state of agitation by stirring storms, and it is deprived of the calm and steadfastness of inner wisdom. In contrast to this it was well said by the prophet, "To whom will my Spirit look, but to him that is humble and quiet, and trembleth at my word" (see Isa 66:2)... The Lord calls us, while we are in these wounds of turmoil, saying, "Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest" (Mt 11:28-29).

28.14.5.en: What is more exhausting than for a man to be feverish with earthly passions? Or what is more restful here than for a man not to desire anything of this world? For this reason the Israelites were given the keeping of the Sabbath as a gift... For the people who follow God receive the Sabbath, that is, the rest of the spirit, by not being entangled in this life, that is, by not being absorbed in carnal pleasures...

28.14.6.en: But how can we know that most of the ancient Fathers held fast to this wisdom in their inner life, while outwardly they were managing the affairs of the world?

28.14.7.en: Shall we reckon Joseph deprived of receiving this wisdom, he upon whose shoulders were laid the affairs of all Egypt in the time of famine, not only to provide for the needs of the Egyptians, but who, by his surpassing skill, also took care to preserve the lives of the foreign people who came to him?

28.14.8.en: Was Daniel a stranger to this wisdom, he who, when he was set as ruler over the governors by the king of the Chaldeans in Babylon, was occupied with great responsibilities...? It is therefore clear that often even the righteous are engaged in earthly obligations without being entangled...

28.14.9.en: Those who have this calm, however troublesome their outward occupations may be, these troubles will not enter into their inner depths... For their hearts are filled with this wisdom, so they are neither entangled nor troubled... The minds troubled by worldly matters cry out simply because they are not at rest and are cut off from true wisdom.

28.15.0.en: 15 It cannot be gotten for gold, neither shall silver be weighed for the price thereof. 16 It cannot be valued with the gold of Ophir, with the precious onyx, or the sapphire. 17 The gold and the crystal cannot equal it: and the exchange of it shall not be for jewels of fine gold. 18 No mention shall be made of coral, or of pearls: for the price of wisdom is above rubies. 19 The topaz of Ethiopia shall not equal it, neither shall it be valued with pure gold.

28.15.1.en: "It cannot be gotten for gold, neither shall silver be weighed for the price thereof" [15].

28.15.2.en: Since the wisdom of God is the Hypostasis of the Word, whoever acquires it acquires the Creator Himself, and there is no ground for comparison between Him and created things, however great their value.

28.15.3.en: * To what does pure gold point but to the angels, who are rightly called pure gold? They are gold because they shine with the splendor of righteousness, and pure gold because no stain of sin has ever touched them. As for human beings, as long as they are in the corruptible flesh and subject to death, they can be gold, but they cannot be pure gold. "The corruptible body presseth down the soul, and the earthly tabernacle weigheth down the mind that museth upon many things" (Wis 9:15). Even in this life they may shine with surpassing splendor of righteousness, and yet they will not be wholly free from the dross of sins. The Apostle John bears witness to this when he says, "If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us" (1 Jn 1:8). James confirms it, saying, "In many things we offend all" (Jas 3:2). In the same way the prophet pleads, saying, "Enter not into judgment with thy servant, O Lord: for in thy sight shall no man living be justified" (Ps 143:2).

28.15.4.en: So Wisdom reveals Himself by Himself, so that the human race may be saved from sin. An angel is not sent in place of Wisdom, for it is necessary that the creature be set free by the Creator. Thus the Lord says in the Gospel, "If the Son therefore shall make you free, ye shall be free indeed" (Jn 8:36).

28.15.5.en: But the holy man (Job), being filled with the spirit of this wisdom, foresaw that Judaism would become the condition of those who put their hope in the giver of the Law and make Moses the source of their salvation, for they spoke evil even to the one who had been healed: "Thou art his disciple; but we are Moses' disciples" (Jn 9:28).

28.16.0.en: "It cannot be valued with the gold of Ophir, with the precious onyx, or the sapphire" [16].

28.16.1.en: In the Septuagint it reads, "It shall not be compared with the dyed colors of India." Pope Gregory (the Great) sees that the wisdom of God is not tainted by the ornament of rhetoric; it would be pleasing like a garment without dye. Paul made light of dye when he said, "Which things also we speak, not in the words which man's wisdom teacheth, but which the Holy Ghost teacheth" (1 Cor 2:13). The Apostle chose to use this wisdom in the simplicity of pure truth alone, without staining it with the dye of speech.

28.17.0.en: "The gold and the crystal cannot equal it: and the exchange of it shall not be for jewels of fine gold" [17].

28.17.1.en: Since the Word of God became incarnate and became man, no man equals Him, whether gold or crystal, however brilliant like gold or transparently pure like crystal.

28.17.2.en: * John saw this in the Revelation when he said, "The building of the wall of it was of jasper: and the city was pure gold, like unto clear glass" (Rev 21:18). This is because all the saints will shine in the splendor of surpassing blessedness; therefore (the heavenly Jerusalem) is described as a building of gold... But as long as we are in this life, and our hearts cannot be seen by others, they are not vessels of glass but vessels of earthenware. In this clay, which can corrupt the mind, the prophet fears lest he sink, when he says, "Deliver me out of the mire, and let me not sink" (Ps 69:14). Paul himself calls the tabernacle of our bodies "our earthly house of this tabernacle," and says, "For we know that if our earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved, we have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens" (2 Cor 5:1)... Yet all the saints shine with such wonderful splendor, and gleam with such surpassing purity, that they become in the likeness of Wisdom, but they do not equal it. For this reason all the saints are brought into the eternal joys so that they may become in the likeness of God, as it is written: "When he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is" (1 Jn 3:2). And yet it is written: "O Lord God of hosts, who is like unto thee?" (Ps 89:8, 6). Also: "Who among the sons of the mighty can be likened unto the Lord?" How can they be like Him, and yet not be like Him, except that they will be like this Wisdom in likeness, but they are not equal to it? They are like Him because they become blessed, and they are not like Him because He is the Creator; they do not equal Him since He is incomprehensible, while they are comprehensible beings. Therefore it may be said with justice, "The gold and the crystal cannot equal it." For however great the splendor and purity with which the saints shine, this belongs to men as those who are wise in God, whereas He is the Wisdom of God, which is another matter...

28.17.3.en: "And the exchange of it shall not be for jewels of fine gold" [17]... The Church will not exchange this Wisdom for precious and lofty vessels of gold, for she holds fast to Christ the Son of God, not as one of the prophets, but as the one Lord of the prophets.

28.17.5.en: * The Son gives Himself, so that He Himself, being righteousness, removes evil from us; Wisdom offers Herself that She may take the place of folly.

28.18.0.en: St. Jerome "No mention shall be made of coral, or of pearls: for the price of wisdom is above rubies" [18].

28.19.0.en: "The topaz of Ethiopia shall not equal it, neither shall it be valued with pure gold" [19].

28.19.1.en: Wisdom is the Lord of glory Jesus, who is more precious than all pearls, coral, crystal, and everything precious.

28.19.2.en: * We have often said that Christ is wisdom, justice, peace, joy, gentleness, and the rest of such things. Note that the names of all these virtues are loved even by those who do not pursue them. There is no criminal who declares shamelessly that he does not love wisdom and justice.

28.20.0.en: 20 "Whence then cometh wisdom? and where is the place of understanding? 21 Seeing it is hid from the eyes of all living, and kept close from the fowls of the air. 22 Destruction and death say, We have heard the fame thereof with our ears. 23 God understandeth the way thereof, and he knoweth the place thereof. 24 For he looketh to the ends of the earth, and seeth under the whole heaven; 25 To make the weight for the winds; and he weigheth the waters by measure. 26 When he made a decree for the rain, and a way for the lightning of the thunder: 27 Then did he see it, and declare it; he prepared it, yea, and searched it out. 28 And unto man he said, Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom; and to depart from evil is understanding.

28.20.1.en: "Whence then cometh wisdom? and where is the place of understanding?" [20].

28.20.2.en: The men of God often cry out, asking for wisdom from the Heavenly One, for whence does wisdom come, and where is the place of understanding, if not from the heavenly God?

28.20.3.en: * He gives knowledge not by a book that we learn from, but by the enlightenment of the Spirit.

28.20.4.en: Ambrosiaster * Those who become small in the flesh, leaving their own knowledge, are the wise in the world... They become of their own free will like infants, learning the wisdom that is not acquired through the toil of study.

28.20.5.en: St. Mar Isaac the Syrian * It comes from the One from whom it proceeds. Now its way is hidden, since it is begotten of the Invisible One, who is co-eternal with the Father. The prophet expressed the "whence" by saying, "Who shall declare his generation?" (Isa 53:8). Now the place of understanding has become the mind of man, the man whom the wisdom of God fills and makes holy...

28.21.0.en: "Seeing it is hid from the eyes of all living, and kept close from the fowls of the air?" [21]

28.21.1.en: The desire of the heart of every believer and every true theologian is that it may be the right of the chosen to enjoy the vision of God in eternal life. This is what St. John the Apostle declares: "For we shall see him as he is" (1 Jn 3:2). Yet in the same epistle he says, "No man hath seen God at any time" (1 Jn 4:12). And the Apostle Paul affirms: "Dwelling in the light which no man can approach unto; whom no man hath seen, nor can see" (1 Tim 6:16). This raises many questions, among them: 1. Is this vision reserved only for eternal life? Or can it begin here in an inner experience in the depths of the soul? 2. Is the vision of God by the heavenly beings a vision of His essence? And do the believers in heaven enjoy the vision of the divine essence?

28.21.2.en: St. John Chrysostom wrote a treatise entitled "The Incomprehensible Nature of God," in which he shows the impossibility of seeing God in His essence as He is. The councils of Constantinople in the fourteenth century (1341, 1351, 1368 AD) affirmed that God cannot be approached with respect to His essence; He is not the object of the knowledge of the angels or the saints, nor the object of their vision, but this divine essence is seen through His uncreated divine energies. Father Gregory Palamas spoke at length about this teaching.

28.21.3.en: * When we hear that the Seraphim fly around the throne in its loftiness and exaltation, covering their faces with two wings... and covering their feet with two, and crying out with a voice full of trembling, do not suppose that they have feathers, feet and wings, for they are invisible powers...

28.21.4.en: Truly God is incomprehensible even to these orders, and they are not able to draw near to Him; therefore He condescends to appear in the manner that is recorded in the vision. For God is not bounded by a place, nor does He sit upon a throne... but His sitting upon the throne and His being surrounded by the heavenly powers is a matter of His love for them.

28.21.5.en: If He appeared on the throne and these powers surrounded Him, they cannot behold Him, nor have they endured to look at the splendor of His light, so they cover their eyes with their wings, and there remains for them only to praise and sing hymns full of glory and holy trembling, and wonderful songs that bear witness to the holiness of Him who sits on the throne.

28.21.6.en: He who dares to examine the providence of God, which the heavenly powers cannot touch or express, ought rather to hide himself, concealed under the hills.

28.21.7.en: St. John Chrysostom Many of the Fathers of the Church and scholars throughout the ages have been occupied with discovering whether the believers will see God as He is or within certain limits.

28.21.8.en: * If Wisdom, who is God, is hidden from the eyes of the living, then certainly none of the saints can see this Wisdom. And I hear John agreeing with this statement: "No man hath seen God at any time" (Jn 1:18).

28.21.9.en: But when I look at the fathers of the Old Testament, I learn that many of them, as the history of Holy Scripture testifies, saw God.

28.21.10.en: For Jacob saw the Lord and said, "For I have seen God face to face" (Gen 32:30).

28.21.11.en: Likewise Moses saw God, of whom it is written, "And the Lord spake unto Moses face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend" (Ex 33:11).

28.21.12.en: Job himself saw the Lord and said, "I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye seeth thee" (Job 42:5).

28.21.13.en: The prophet Isaiah saw the Lord and said, "In the year that king Uzziah died I saw also the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up" (Isa 6:1).

28.21.14.en: Micaiah saw the Lord, saying, "I saw the Lord sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven standing by him on his right hand and on his left" (1 Kgs 22:19).

28.21.15.en: What then does it mean that many fathers of the Old Testament testify that they saw God, and yet it is said concerning this Wisdom, who is God, "It is hid from the eyes of all living" (Job 28:21), and John says, "No man hath seen God at any time" (Jn 1:18)? It is clear to us that, as long as we live here a mortal life, God can be seen by means of appearances, but seeing Him truly in His nature cannot be achieved.

28.22.0.en: We have heard the fame thereof with our ears" [22].

28.22.1.en: Pope Gregory (the Great) sees that destruction and death refer to the evil spirits that cause ruin and destruction, for it is said of Satan, "His name was Death" (Rev 6:8). These spirits do not see Wisdom, since they were driven out from before Him because of their pride, and became unable to see the wisdom of God. "They are of those that rebel against the light; they know not the ways thereof, nor abide in the paths thereof" (see Job 24:13).

28.23.0.en: "God understandeth the way thereof, and he knoweth the place thereof" [23].

28.23.1.en: None knows the divine Wisdom, or the Son, except the Father. He knows the way of Wisdom, because He is begotten of Him eternally; there is no separation between the Father and the Son.

28.23.2.en: * Wisdom, co-eternal with God, has its way in one sense and its place in another... The place of Wisdom is the Father, and the place of the Father is Wisdom, as Wisdom Himself testifies, saying, "I am in the Father, and the Father in me" (Jn 14:10).

28.23.4.en: "For he looketh to the ends of the earth,

28.24.0.en: and seeth under the whole heaven" [24].

28.24.1.en: * The seeing of God is the renewal of His grace for things that were lost and corrupted. Therefore it is written: "A king that sitteth in the throne of judgment scattereth away all evil with his eyes" (Prov 20:8). By His seeing He puts an end to the evils of our folly, and grants great esteem to maturity.

28.25.0.en: "To make the weight for the winds; and he weigheth the waters by measure" [25].

28.25.1.en: * In Holy Scripture the speed and lightness of the wind generally point to souls. As the Psalmist of God says, "Who walketh upon the wings of the wind" (Ps 104:3), meaning, who goes above the virtues of the soul. Accordingly, "He makes the weight for the winds," meaning that the wisdom from above fills souls, making them heavy with maturity, and not with the weight of which it is said, "O ye sons of men, how long will ye turn my glory into shame?" (Ps 4:2) ["how long will your hearts be heavy"]. For to be weighed down by (good) counsel is one thing, and to be weighed down by sin is another; to be weighed down by obligation is one thing, and to be weighed down by transgression is another...

28.25.2.en: "And he weigheth the waters by measure" [25]. In Holy Scripture waters are used to point to the Holy Spirit, sometimes they are used of false knowledge, sometimes of calamities and swept-away peoples, and sometimes of those who follow the faith. Thus water points to the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, as it is said in the Gospel: "He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water." And the Evangelist adds, "But this spake he of the Spirit, which they that believe on him should receive" (Jn 7:38-39). Again water points to holy knowledge, as it is said: "With the water of wisdom shall she give him to drink" (Sir 15:3). Likewise water points to evil knowledge, like the woman mentioned by Solomon who bears a symbol of heresy and who bewitches with her deceiving arts, so it is said: "Stolen waters are sweet" (Prov 9:17).

28.25.3.en: Likewise the expression "waters" points to trials, as the Psalmist says, "Save me, O God; for the waters are come in unto my soul" (Ps 69:1) ("Save me, O God; for the waters are come in unto my soul").

28.25.4.en: The waters also point to peoples, as it is said by John: "The waters... are peoples" (Rev 17:15). So also not only the sweeping tide of peoples, but also the minds of the righteous who follow the preaching of the faith, as in the saying of the prophet, "Blessed are ye that sow beside all waters" (Isa 32:20), and the saying of the Psalmist, "The voice of the Lord is upon the waters" (Ps 29:3).

28.25.5.en: In this place, to what does the title "waters" point but to the hearts of the chosen, who through the understanding of wisdom receive the hearing of the heavenly voice?

28.26.0.en: "When he made a decree for the rain, and a way (and a path) for the lightning of the thunder" [26].

28.26.1.en: * By the rains he points to the words of the preachers; therefore it is said of Moses, "My doctrine shall drop as the rain" (Deut 32:2). That is, when they present my words with gentle persuasion it is rain, and when they thunder about terrifying matters concerning the coming judgment they utter voices like crashing thunders...

28.26.2.en: The authority of speech is lost when the voice is not supported by deed. It is said by the Psalmist: "But unto the wicked God saith, What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth? Seeing thou hatest instruction, and casttest my words behind thee" (Ps 50:16-17)... This was written about the law of preaching: "Whosoever therefore shall break one of these least commandments, and shall teach men so, he shall be called the least in the kingdom of heaven: but whosoever shall do and teach them, the same shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven," of whom it is written: "They shall gather out of his kingdom all things that offend, and them which do iniquity" (Mt 13:41). For in the heavenly Kingdom it is necessary that the "things that offend" be gathered out and cast out... Now He made [a way for the crashing thunders] [26] when He establishes contact with the hearts of men struck with dread of the coming judgment by His preachers.

28.27.0.en: "Then did he see it, and declare it; he prepared it, yea, and searched it out" [27].

28.27.1.en: Pope Gregory (the Great) sees that it is fitting for us to notice that there are four things concerning wisdom, when he says, "Then did he see it, and declare it; he prepared it, yea, and searched it out" [27].

28.27.2.en: * He sees it as being "the likeness," and declares it as it is "the Word," and prepares it as it is "the remedy," and searches it out as being "hidden from sight." The eternal wisdom of God is the image of the Father and His Word, when the mind of man penetrates it. So whoever wishes to understand it must understand it as the Word without time, and the Image without limit.

28.27.4.en: It is fitting that the wisdom of God absorb our whole being, our feelings and our senses.

28.27.5.en: * If Christ is the head of the believer, then "the wise man's eyes are in his head" (Eccl 2:14). Consequently all our senses, our mind, our thoughts, our word and our counsels (if we are wise) are centered in Christ.

28.28.0.en: St. Jerome "And unto man he said, Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom; and to depart from evil is understanding" [28].

28.28.1.en: St. Augustine comments on this phrase, saying that the Greek word θεοσέβεια (theosebeia), which is sometimes translated "godliness": [Behold, godliness, that is wisdom], means "the worship of God." The main point in worship is that the soul not be ungrateful to God. Therefore the truly excellent sacrifice is to offer thanksgiving to God our Lord. Wisdom is the inner thanksgiving of the soul toward God, which it expresses by spiritual worship of Him.

28.28.2.en: Again he affirms that whoever ascribes wisdom to himself is not thankful to God, and therefore does not bear the fear of the Lord and is not godly; he is foolish and not wise.

28.28.3.en: * "Behold, godliness, that is wisdom; and to depart from evil is understanding" (Job 28:28). Here is the distinction (between wisdom and understanding), for we must understand that wisdom belongs to contemplation, and understanding belongs to action. In this place by wisdom he means the worship of God... And what is the worship of God but love for God, by which we long to see Him, and believe and hope to see Him in part? As we progress we see as in a mirror, in a riddle, but then the vision will be in clarity... As for departing from evil, which Job says is understanding, it undoubtedly concerns temporal matters. For with regard to time (in this world) we are in evil, from which we must cease until we attain the eternal goods.

28.28.4.en: * There is another kind of wicked, who when they knew God, glorified him not as God, neither were thankful (Rom 1:21). In this "I also fell, but thy right hand held me up" (Ps 18:35), and bore me far away, and set me where I could be healed. For You said to man: "Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom" (Job 28:28), and "be not wise in thine own eyes" (Prov 3:7), for "professing themselves to be wise, they became fools" (Rom 1:22). But now I have found the pearl of great price, for which I needed to sell all and buy it (Mt 13:46), but I hesitated.

28.28.5.en: * If knowledge is of the right kind, it is the handmaid of love, for without love "knowledge puffeth up" (1 Cor 8:1), but where love is, it fills the heart with edification, so that knowledge finds nothing empty that it could puff up. Add to this that Job shows useful knowledge by defining it afterward when he says, "the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom," adding, "and to depart from evil is understanding."

28.28.6.en: * "Behold, the worship of God is wisdom." Then the mind is wise, not by its own light, but by participation in that exalted light, which is eternal, in which it reigns in blessedness.

28.28.7.en: St. Augustine * "Behold, godliness, that is wisdom; and to depart from evil is understanding" [28]. There is nothing like this practical training, nothing stronger than this wisdom. "The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge, and a good understanding have all they that do his commandments" (see Prov 1:7). This is the greatest of possessions. The honoring of God is the supreme wisdom.

28.28.8.en: St. John Chrysostom * O man, return to yourself. Examine the secrets of your heart, and if you find that you fear the Lord, it is truly evident that you are full of wisdom... This wisdom, which is awesome in itself even to the angels, is called in you "the fear of the Lord." For you truly possess wisdom if you fear the Lord.

28.28.10.en: May I acquire You, O divine Wisdom!

28.28.11.en: * You gave man a mind, that he might search and work.

28.28.12.en: By human wisdom he is able to search for precious metals, but in foolishness he does not seek the mysteries of the Kingdom of God.

28.28.13.en: Grant me to discover the silver of Your pure wisdom, and to acquire the gold, the pledge of the heavenly life.

28.28.14.en: * Man brings silver and gold out of the dust and the stones.

28.28.15.en: Let there come forth from me, who am dust, a witness to You, and let me become in Your eyes more precious than every precious stone!

28.28.16.en: You are able to turn dust into heaven,

28.28.17.en: and the heart of stone into a heart enlarged with love.

28.28.18.en: * You are the worker of wonders and miracles.

28.28.19.en: You brought forth from Saul of Tarsus a unique apostle,

28.28.20.en: and from the wicked people of Nineveh a repentant people,

28.28.21.en: and from the Gentiles a holy Church.

28.28.22.en: You made man out of dust, and from the earthy sinner You raise up a being like the angels!

28.28.23.en: * Behold, I am in Your hands; establish Your Kingdom within me.

28.28.24.en: Embrace me, as it were, among the ranks of Your angels,

28.28.25.en: that I may be in touch with Your love, and know Your divine mysteries.

28.28.26.en: You are the way that brings me into the bosom of the Father.

28.28.27.en: You are my riches and my joy!

28.28.28.en: * May I acquire You, O divine Wisdom!

28.28.29.en: In You I enter into the mysteries of heaven, and enjoy partaking of the divine nature.

28.28.30.en: In You my eyes are opened, and I see what no eye has seen.

28.28.31.en: * For the sake of acquiring wealth, man learned the craft of mining,

28.28.32.en: and because of hunger the lion came to know the ways of the forests and the wilds,

28.28.33.en: and for the sake of being fed, the eagles see the prey from lofty distances.

28.28.34.en: And for the sake of love I acquire You, and You present to me the surpassing divine mysteries.

28.28.35.en: * Your wisdom is mighty and surpassing.

28.28.36.en: You bring me into the impossible, and reveal to me wonders beyond measure!

28.28.37.en: You lift the humble up to heaven.

28.28.38.en: You turn stones into children of Abraham!

28.28.39.en: And You shake those who hold authority and power!

28.28.40.en: You cause a spring of sweet waters of love to well up from my rocky heart!

28.28.41.en: You make me very precious in Your eyes, O Lover of mankind!

28.28.42.en: * May I acquire You, O wondrous Wisdom of God,

28.28.43.en: that I may carry within me the treasure of all wisdom, knowledge and understanding.

28.28.45.en: No gold, nor silver, nor precious stones can be compared with You.

28.28.46.en: * Behold, all of nature with all its creativity cries out to me:

28.28.47.en: Acquire Creativity itself, Beauty itself, the Creator of all and the Maker of everything!

28.28.48.en: * How marvelous You are, hidden and present.

28.28.49.en: Your mysteries are hidden even from the Cherubim, who cover their faces because of the greatness of Your splendor!

28.28.50.en: You hid Yourself from me for a time, not to deprive me of You, but to inflame my heart with longing for You.

28.28.51.en: You became incarnate and came down to me, so that I find You within me!

28.28.52.en: You are very near to me!

28.28.53.en: My depths cry out to You:
